prompt:
An angle has a measure of $\frac{(5\pi )}{6}$ radians. What is the measure of the angle, in degrees? (Disregard the degree symbol when entering your answer.)

$$0$$

$$150$$
explanation: The correct answer is $150$. The measure of an angle, in degrees, can be found by multiplying its measure, in radians, by $\frac{180\text{ degrees}}{\pi\text{ radians}}$. Multiplying the given angle measure, $\frac{5\pi}{6}$ radians, by $\frac{180\text{ degrees}}{\pi\text{ radians}}$ yields $\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\text{ radians}\right)\left(\frac{180\text{ degrees}}{\pi\text{ radians}}\right)$. The $\pi$ terms cancel, giving $\frac{5 \times 180}{6}\text{ degrees}$. This simplifies to $\frac{900}{6}\text{ degrees}$, which equals $150$ degrees.
